what: Deutsche Bank is Germany's largest bank. It serves German households and companies, finances corporates across Europe, and runs a large fixed income trading and investment banking business, plus the asset manager DWS.
customers: German retail and business customers, European and global corporations, institutional investors and governments.
money: fixed income and currency trading, debt origination and advisory
transaction banking, lending and cash management for companies
German retail banking and wealth management
moat: The home relationship with German industry and one of the few European banks able to compete in global fixed income trading.
risks: Trading revenue is volatile and capital-intensive
European banks earn lower returns than US rivals
Past conduct and control failures brought large fines
German economic weakness affects its home lending book
opportunities: Profitability has improved after years of restructuring
Higher interest rates lifted income from its deposit base
It has resumed dividends and buybacks after a long gap
watch: Return on tangible equity against its target, and the cost-income ratio.
